newsitem.title: USA: News Corp files suit to block Time-Turner.
newsitem.headline: News Corp files suit to block Time-Turner.

text.p: News Corp Ltd filed a lawsuit Wednesday seeking to block the proposed merger of Time Warner Inc and Turner Broadcasting Systems Inc, contending those companies and Ted Turner were intent on stifling competition from its Fox News Channel.

In the lawsuit filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, News Corp asks for $1 billion in punitive damages for alleged violations of antitrust laws and to compensate for damages it said Fox News suffered when Time Warner reneged on a promise to carry the new 24-hour channel on its cable television network.

News Corp contends it had an agreement with Time Warner to carry the news channel. That agreement was reversed, it said, after Ted Turner, founder of Turner Broadcasting, urged Time Warner to back out of the deal.
Time Warner President Richard Parsons said through a spokesman: "This lawsuit is utter foolishness."
A spokesman for Turner Broadcasting could not be reached immediately for comment.

Time Warner has refused to carry Fox News Service. Instead, it carries two Cable News Network services owned by Turner, and MSNBC, a joint venture of General Electric Co's NBC unit and Microsoft Corp.

"By advising Fox News just three weeks prior to its planned launch date for the Fox News Channel that it would not perform its agreement and carry the (channel), Time Warner has made it impossible for Fox News to achieve the widespread distribution of the (channel) in New York City and in other areas that were important to (its) launch strategy," according to the lawsuit.
Time Warner holds cable-television franchises serving 1.2 million residents of New York. The franchises are set to expire in 1998.
